correctness.rationale: The causal response solves R=1+F*R for uniform interarrival law F on [0,τ]. The two affine barriers are Volterra sub- and supersolutions; local factorial convergence justifies comparison, and R(0)=1 gives sharpness. Independently, Wald's identity gives R(t)=2(t+E[overshoot])/τ, and conditional on the gap before the crossing the crossing increment is uniform on the permitted terminal subinterval, so the conditional mean overshoot is no larger than τ/2. The nonarithmetic key renewal theorem applied to g(t)=E[(U−t)_+] gives mean overshoot limit ∫g/E[U]=τ/3, hence response offset 2/3. Itô covariance and the barrier give precisely 4Dst/τ+2Ds and the variance coefficients. Under Brownian scaling the shared-noise kernel difference is e(Tv)/T with 0≤e≤1; the isometry and dominated convergence give 2Dt/T² and the limiting coefficient 8Dt/9 at fixed τ. For tightness, the response equation and barrier already give |R′(t)|≤3/τ for t>τ, and R=e^{t/τ} before τ, so the scaled kernels are uniformly Lipschitz. Splitting the old and fresh noise gives variance increments O(|t−s|) and Gaussian fourth moments O(|t−s|²). The finite method-of-steps checker in checks/verify.py was located and inspected, not run. No path-supremum L² estimate or nonlinear result follows.
